sections.h2: Where does a Lancaster County deed get recorded, and until what hour?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Recorder of Deeds at 150 North Queen Street, Suite 315, Lancaster, PA 17603. The office is open from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, and recording itself concludes at 4:30 p.m.

The county's recorder website notes that payments are not taken over the phone. It also says that since October 1, 2025 staff no longer print trusts or other supporting papers as a courtesy, so a submitter who wants to skip a 25 cent per page printing charge must send those pages already printed, or attach them to an electronic filing.

For a seller, this office comes at the very end. The deed is signed and acknowledged at closing, then recorded here, and the county's public search shows the new owner afterward.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Lancaster County?
sections.html:
The posted base fee for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages is $71.25. Every page after the fourth adds $2.00, and the office says it does not issue refunds.

Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds base fees, up to four pages, from the office's fee schedule
Document typeBase fee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Assignment, release, satisfaction, installment sale agreement, easement$59.75
Agreement, termination, modification, subordination$58.75
Power of attorney or deputation (miscellaneous)$18.50
Certification$10.00
Copies, per page$0.25

The recorder's bulletin board adds that the JCP fee rose from $40.25 to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025. Because that line sits on the home page and the fee page lists a round base figure, call the office for the exact total on your package.

A veteran's discharge, the DD-214, is recorded free.

sections.h2: How should I pay at the Lancaster County recorder's counter?
sections.html:
Cash, certified checks, corporate checks, money orders and credit cards are accepted to record documents. Personal checks are refused for amounts over $75 and are never taken for transfer tax. Blank checks are not accepted either.

  • Card payments carry a 2.5% charge on transactions over $50, and $1 on smaller ones.
  • A returned check costs $25.00.
  • There are no refunds, so the amount has to be right the first time.
  • Mailed or couriered packages need a self-addressed stamped envelope of the right size and with enough postage.

The county says that when a document type has no listed fee, the Recorder sets one. If your deed has attachments or several parcels, ask before sending money.

sections.h2: What rules does Lancaster County apply to the deed itself?
sections.html:
Cover pages are no longer required, and staples are banned. Documents go on white 8.5 by 11 paper in type no smaller than 10 point.

  • The notary acknowledgment date cannot come before the date on the document, and the acknowledgment needs the state, county, date, the person appearing, the notary's signature and the notary's expiration date. The seal itself is optional for Pennsylvania notaries.
  • The tax parcel ID, with its district code, must appear on every deed.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments need a signed, certified address with a zip code for the buyer or lender. On a deed a P.O. box is not allowed as that address, though the deed may say tax bills should go to a box.
  • Land in more than one municipality must state the percentage split of local transfer tax, in whole numbers.
  • Written amounts must match numbers, and no Social Security or bank account numbers should appear.
  • A transaction is limited to 10 documents, and blanket assignments or releases are rejected.

Corrective or confirmatory deeds need a Statement of Value, an explanation and a full copy of the deed being fixed.

sections.h2: How does Pennsylvania realty transfer tax work in Lancaster County?
sections.html:
The Recorder collects it at the same moment the deed is recorded. The Commonwealth's rate is 1 percent of the transferred value, and the Department of Revenue holds both buyer and seller liable. Local taxes are collected alongside it and shared by municipalities and school districts.

Exemptions exist for certain family transfers, transfers to governments, and property passing by will or intestate succession. Whenever tax is not paid in full, a fully completed Statement of Value must accompany the deed, and the county counts that form as a page toward the four-page base. Easements need one too.

The office also warns that a deed with the wrong property location is the submitter's responsibility. The correct tax must go to the right municipality, school district and state, and the submitter has to claim any refund from the places paid by mistake.

sections.h2: What is Lancaster County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lancaster County spans 984 square miles, of which 944 are land, and it was carved out of Chester County on May 10, 1729. The 2020 census counted 552,984 residents, the sixth-highest total among Pennsylvania counties. Lancaster city is the seat; Ephrata, Elizabethtown, Columbia, Lititz and Millersville are among the larger boroughs. Farmland, the Amish community and tourism shape much of the county.

Rain falls on about 124 days a year, around 44 inches in all, with roughly 21 inches of snow, according to NOAA normals reported for Lancaster. Basements and roofs take the weather, and buyers will look at both.

sections.h2: What else does the Lancaster County recorder file besides deeds?
sections.html:
The office handles mortgages, satisfactions, assignments, powers of attorney, leases, Uniform Commercial Code filings, notary commissions and veterans' discharges. Several of these touch a house sale, so know the charges ahead of time.

  • A notary commission and bond costs $32.00, and registering the notary's signature adds $4.75.
  • Subdivision, stormwater and state highway plans start at $15.00 for the first page and add $2.00 per page; condominium plans start at $30.00.
  • Plans must be at least 18 by 24 inches and no larger than 24 by 36, and both Mylar and paper are accepted.
  • A UCC-1 or UCC-3 filing costs $100.00 each.
  • Notaries can register their signature at the Recorder's office, which saves a trip to the Prothonotary's office in a separate building.

A seller paying off a mortgage should ask the lender when the satisfaction piece will be filed. At the posted $59.75 base, it is a separate recording with its own book and page reference back to the original mortgage.

sections.h2: What should I check before the deed leaves for the courthouse?
sections.html:
Run through these items with the title agent.

  • Parcel ID and district code on the deed, matching the county record.
  • A certified buyer address that is not a P.O. box.
  • Dollar figures that agree in words and numbers.
  • A completed Statement of Value if the transfer is taxed in part or exempt.
  • Payment in an accepted form: no personal check over $75 and none at all for transfer tax.
  • No staples and no cover sheet.

If the deed is going by mail, put the package together a few days early and enclose the return envelope. The office's public records search lets you confirm afterward that the deed appears under the buyer's name.

faqs.q: What is the base fee for a deed at the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The posted base fee is $71.25 for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages, plus $2.00 for each added page. The recorder's bulletin says the JCP fee rose to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025, so confirm the total with the office.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lancaster County transfer tax with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks are not accepted for the payment of transfer tax, and they are refused for any amount over $75. Use cash, a certified or corporate check, a money order or a credit card, with the card fee added.

faqs.q: Does a Lancaster County deed need a cover page?
faqs.a: No. Cover pages are no longer required, and staples must not be used. Use white 8.5 by 11 paper and type of at least 10 point.

faqs.q: Can I use a P.O. box as the buyer's address on a Lancaster County deed?
faqs.a: No. The certified grantee address on a deed cannot be a P.O. box. You may state on the deed that tax bills should be mailed to a P.O. box, but the certified address must be a street address with a zip code.

faqs.q: What time does the Lancaster County recorder stop recording?
faqs.a: Recording concludes at 4:30 p.m., though the office remains open until 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. Documents that come in after 4:30 p.m. wait for the next business day.
